theory_title: The rules that change the arithmetic
theory_content: Gains on virtual digital assets are taxed at a flat 30% with no deduction except the cost of acquisition, losses cannot be set off against any other income or carried forward, and 1% TDS applies on each transfer above the threshold. A strategy that trades frequently loses 1% to TDS each time and cannot net its losses, which changes the maths far more than most people account for.

On an exchange, the exchange holds the keys and you hold a claim against it — which is exactly what failed at FTX. In a self-custodied wallet, you hold the keys and an irrecoverable loss is entirely your own. There is no third option and no deposit insurance in either case. The trade-off is counterparty risk against operational risk.

theory_title: Why position size is the entire risk decision
theory_content: Bitcoin has fallen more than 70% from a peak on several occasions and recovered on some of them. Any allocation must be small enough that a total loss changes nothing about your plan — commonly 1-5% for people who want exposure. The asset’s volatility is not the risk; the position size is.

Gold has returned roughly 9-10% a year in rupee terms over long periods, much of that from rupee depreciation rather than the metal. It has no cash flow, so it cannot be valued the way a business can; its role is as a hedge that often rises when equity falls. Sovereign gold bonds add 2.5% annual interest and avoid making charges and storage.
